summary: Burkhard Quessel is a tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was attested as a member in 1997. He served as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).

Burton Watson (1925–2017) was a sinologist and japanologist who studied at Columbia University (~1948–1956). He held posts at Kyoto University (~1952–1956), Columbia University as professor (~1961–1973), and Stanford University (~1964–1965).

Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima (1898–1959) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery under Thubten Nyendrak and Khenpo Genam, and later taught Khenpo Chökhyap, Khenpo Dazer, Jigme Phuntsok, and Tarthang Tulku.

C. D. Sebastian is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, studied under Paul Williams, Gavin D'Costa, Ashok Kumar Chatterjee, and Abhimanyu Singh, and was attested as Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay in 2016.

C. F. Lee (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1970) and the University of Western Ontario (~1970–1972), later serving as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong (1994–2015).

C. Kunhan Raja (1895–1963) was an Indologist who served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1927 and 1946. His students included K. Kunjunni Raja, Madhav Krishna Sharma, and H. G. Narahari.
C. R. Krishnamacharlu (born 1888) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his F. A. at Madras Christian College and earned a university degree at Pachaiyappa's College.
C. S. Srinivasachariar (1890–1951) was an Indologist and historian who served as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).
C. S. Sundaram was an Indologist who taught Tomy Augustine. He held posts at The Madras Sanskrit College and at the University of Madras, where he was Reader in Sanskrit in 1951.

C. W. Huntington (1949–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, and was a professor at Hartwick College (~2000–2020).

Calambur Sivaramamurti (1910–1983) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Presidency University, Kolkata (~1928–1934) under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He worked at the Government Museum, Chennai (1935–1946), the Indian Museum (1946), and the National Museum, New Delhi (attested 1952).

Calvert Watkins (1933–2013) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1950–1959). He held faculty posts at Harvard University (1959–2003) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2003–2013).

Cameron Bailey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Indiana University, Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, Jimmy Yu, Kathleen M. Erndl, and Joseph Hellweg, and at the University of Oxford under Ulrike Roesler.
Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a PhD at Harvard University under Yudru Tsomu. He held posts at Middlebury College and Dickinson College.
Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology who completed an MA at Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2018).

Camillo Alessio Formigatti is an Indologist who studied at the University of Milan. He worked on the Sanskrit Manuscripts Project at the University of Cambridge (2011–2014), taught Sanskrit at SOAS, and served as Sanskrit Librarian at the Bodleian Libraries (attested 2019).

Carl Bielefeldt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying under Shunryu Suzuki (~1967–1971) and earning a PhD at UC Berkeley (~1974–1980), he served on the editorial board at Stanford University (~1980–2013) and joined the Numata Center (attested 2017).

Carl Cappeller (1840–1925) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied in Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, at Königsberg, Leipzig (PhD ~1868), and Jena (Habilitation 1872), where he became a professor in 1875 and taught Carl Gaedicke.

Carl Friedrich Gauss (1777–1855) studied at Collegium Carolinum (1792–1795), the University of Göttingen (1795–1798), and the University of Helmstedt (~1798–1799). He held a post at the University of Göttingen (~1807–1855), where he taught Moritz Abraham Stern.
Carl Gaedicke was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Jena in 1877, having studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.
